Basic-attack SFX dispatcher  (melee_attack_sfx_dispatch)
------------------------------------------------------------
a0 = action context, a1 = phase. The sound is keyed off the
EQUIPPED WEAPON, not the unit sprite:
  graphic = u8[ctx+0x1ab]              ; equipped weapon `graphic` id
  s2      = u8[ weapon_graphic_soundclass_ptr(graphic) + 5 ]   ; sound class
  if s2 >= 0x20: s2 = 1                ; clamp
phase 0  -> play attack_swing_sfx_by_class[s2]      ; swing / windup whoosh
phase 1  -> loop the action's hit entries; switch u8[entry+0x18e]:
             cases 2,3,a   -> attack_block_sfx_by_class[s2]
             cases 9,c     -> attack_hit_sfx_by_class[s2]  (or 0x72 if u8[tgt+0x18d])
             cases 1,4,7,b,d -> 0x30 (Blade Grasp, hardcoded)
             cases 6,8     -> (no sound)
Verified live in PCSX (2026-06-11): a ninja dual-wielding a Dagger
(graphic 1) + Mythril Knife (graphic 2) produced keys 0x01/0x02 -> both
class 1; a Rune Blade (graphic 0x13) -> class 3. So knife+dagger of one
family share a sound; an archer holding a sword would slash, not twang.
Ranged (bow/crossbow) projectile sound is a SEPARATE path -> see
ranged_charge_sfx_select (FUN_800689a4).

Tile-cursor bob renderer  (tile_cursor_bob_render)  [ADR-0046]
------------------------------------------------------------
Plays the on-grid knife/dagger cursor's at-rest vertical bob from a
ROM step table -- NOT a sine. Two parallel 8-entry int32 tables:
  offset[8] @ 0x80067798 = {0,1,2,3,5,3,2,1}   ; Y offset, FFT units (1 tile = 28)
  hold[8]   @ 0x800677b8 = {16,8,2,2,6,4,4,10} ; frames to dwell per step (cycle = 52)
Both are copied to the stack, then the phase machine advances:
  if (g_cursor_anim_pause @ 0x800960f0 == 1) skip advance   ; bob frozen
  else accum @ 0x800961f4 += g_anim_speed (DAT_80045980, =1 normal play)
       if accum >= hold[phase]: phase++ ; accum = 0 ; phase &= wrap-at-8
The motion is ONE-SIDED from the resting pose (16-frame dwell at offset 0,
single excursion to 5, return) -- not a centered oscillation. The chosen
offset is subtracted from the cursor sprite's world Y (a3 - offset) before
rotate_vector projects it. Pace is 60 Hz +1/frame in normal play.
Static only (disasm + raw-byte cross-check; no probe). The bob DIRECTION
sign and the N=1 tick rate are the two capture-only unknowns (one full
cycle = 52 ticks). Godot reimplementation: TileCursor + CursorBob (the
repo mirrors offset/28 -> world units via PSX_SCALE).

SMALL HUD digit font draw  (draw_number_small_font)
------------------------------------------------------------
Draws a decimal value using FFT's SMALL menu/number font. Per digit:
  U = (value % 10) * 6 + 0x78      ; base 120, pitch 6  (0x78 imm @ 0x8014b0dc/0x8014b1a0)
  glyph cell = 6 wide x 10 tall, sampled at font V = 0x10 (16)
into the small glyph descriptor (hud_small_glyph_descriptor @ 0x80169780:
W=6, H=0xa, stride=0x100=256), then blitted via hud_font_blit (0x8014bae4).
Font source = hud_digit_font_4bpp @ 0x8014d5d4 (4bpp, 256-wide), which is
BYTE-IDENTICAL to EVENT/FRAME.BIN's top rows.

This IS the font of the bottom-left HP/MP/CT readout: build_unit_vitals_window
(0x801363dc) draws cur AND max with THIS routine, so the whole readout is one
size -- the max is merely staggered a baseline lower-right, which reads as a
fraction. There is no separate "big cur" in the vitals.

Cross-validated: the U formula reproduces the small-set glyph origins measured
in FRAME.BIN (120,126,132,..,180) exactly, and the Godot reimplementation
(NumberFont / parse_frame_font.py) renders the panel matching a real PSX
framebuffer. See godot-learning/docs/frame-bin-number-font.md.

Unit vitals window builder  (build_unit_vitals_window)
------------------------------------------------------------
Builds the bottom-left in-battle HP/MP/CT readout (portrait + gradient bars +
numbers). Draws each stat's cur/max via draw_number_small_font (0x8014aec0) --
the SMALL digit font -- so every number in this panel is one size; max staggers
a baseline below cur. Vital display values come from the unit struct
(e.g. unit+0x24, unit+0x26 -> DAT_8014d084/0x8014d086).

The number font is the same one stored in EVENT/FRAME.BIN (RANGETILE.tga, the
BATTLE range-tile/menu atlas, == FRAME.BIN[rows 32:288] pixel-exact; the digit
font lives only in FRAME.BIN's extra top 32 rows). All glyphs render through the
menu CLUT 0x7cbc, same as the Hp/Mp/Ct labels.
See godot-learning/docs/frame-bin-number-font.md.

Event-script opcode 0x11 Unit Anim handler  (evt0x11_unit_anim_handler)
------------------------------------------------------------
Dispatched from BATTLE_block_start_event_instruction (0x8013e904) case body
at 0x8013ead4. a0 = pointer to the 5-byte param payload immediately after
the 0x11 opcode byte in the cinematic event chunk (chunk base 0x8004A6BC):

  +0x00  u16 chunk_unit_id  (LE)  e.g. 0x0034 = Ovelia EVTCHR id
  +0x02  u16 anim_id        (LE)  e.g. 0x025B = cinematic gesture
  +0x04  u8  flag                  0 -> unset_misc_data_move_flag_bit_1
                                   1 -> flip_misc_data_move_flag_bit_1
                                   else -> no-op

Flow:
  1. BATTLE_load_event_command_bytes reads chunk_unit_id from payload[0..1]
  2. resolve_event_unit_handle (0x80147928) resolves chunk_unit_id -> u16 unit_handle.
     Verified live: 0x0034 -> 0x0001 (Ovelia mapped to scenario slot 1).
     Verified live: 0x000C -> 0x000C (Agrias passthrough, narrator slot).
  3. Loop via FUN_801479ac over each matched unit (up to 0x15 iterations):
     - read flag byte from payload+4
     - call the appropriate move-flag-bit-1 helper
  4. BATTLE_load_event_command_bytes reads anim_id from payload+2 (advances reader)
  5. Call BATTLE_set_unit_anim_value(unit_handle, anim_s16)
      -> which (for anim>=0x1F4) falls through to trigger_unit_animations_by_param
      -> which calls set_unit_animation_with_flags(anim, lh(unit_ptr+0x70)=facing, unit_ptr)

Verified unit struct fields (from 0x800B7748 = Ovelia, 0x800BA608 = unit 0x000C):
  +0x00  prev_ptr (linked list)
  +0x04  u8 sprite_lo, u8 team_flag (e.g. 01 02 for Ovelia)
  +0x06  u16 chunk_evtchr_id  <-- ORIGIN chunk_unit_id before remap (Ovelia 0x0034)
  +0x0C  u16 current_anim_slot (0x0014 / 0x0016 observed)
  +0x10  sprite/CLUT reference
  +0x70  s16 current_facing (12-bit angle space)
  +0x74  u16 facing_target (12-bit: 0x000=S 0x400=E 0x800=W 0xC00=N)

Verified live 2026-06-24 from reference-assets/orbonne_prayer_mid_dialog.sstate
+ 1 D press: 2 calls fired consuming the per-unit cmd queue (chunk dispatcher
had already advanced past these opcodes pre-savestate).

Note: unit struct +0x06 holds the chunk_evtchr_id origin (the pre-remap
chunk_unit_id) -- the source of truth for which actor a cinematic anim id
belongs to. (Attributing specific anim-id ranges to named cast members was
contested across notes and is intentionally omitted; ground-truth +0x06 per
scene instead.)

Event-script opcode 0x2D Rotate Unit handler  (evt0x2D_rotate_unit_handler)
------------------------------------------------------------
Dispatched from BATTLE_block_start_event_instruction (0x8013e904) case
body at LAB_8013ec10. a0 = pointer to the 5-byte param payload past the
0x2D opcode byte:

  +0x00  u16 chunk_unit_id  (LE)
  +0x02  u8  Facing         mode selector + 16-direction angle
  +0x03  u8  Direction      rotation direction (CW/CCW/shortest?)
  +0x04  u8  Speed          interp speed; lookup in DAT_80169750
  +0x05  u8  Delay          frames to delay before starting

Facing byte modes (verified live + hacktics disasm):

  0x10            Camera-relative. Reads BATTLE_wrap_camera_yaw_angle()
                  & 0xC00, shifts to a 2-bit cardinal index, looks up
                  DAT_80169754[cardinal] * 4 as the target angle byte.

  0x11/0x12/0x13  Relative rotation: target_byte =
                  BATTLE_get_current_facing_byte_from_misc_id(handle)
                  + (Facing & 0xF) * 4
                  (so 0x11 = +4 nibbles = +90 deg, 0x13 = +12 = +270 deg)

  0x14            Face-the-resolved-target (look-at the resolved handle's
                  position; uses the unit-id-to-coord path).

  otherwise       Absolute: target_12bit_angle = Facing * 0x100. A
                  16-direction wheel with 22.5 deg steps:
                    0x00=S  0x04=E  0x08=W  0x0C=N  intermediates by 22.5
                  Verified live 2026-06-24 via sstate9 BEFORE/AFTER
                  +0x70 diff: Facing=0x02 -> +0x70 went 0xC00 -> 0x200;
                  Facing=0x04 -> +0x70 went 0xC00 -> 0x400. The doc's
                  prior `bitmask` framing (0x09, 0x0D didn't fit) is
                  superseded.

Output: writes a 7-byte pending-rotate command at
  0x8016d9d8 + handle * 7  (pending_rotate_command_array):
    +0  Facing byte (after mode transform)
    +1  Direction
    +2  DAT_80169750[Speed]
    +3  0
    +4  1
    +5  0  (cleared)
    +6  (Delay * incrementing_counter) >> 2

The per-frame tick consumer rotate_command_tick_consumer (0x8013f20c)
reads this and steps unit+0x70 from current toward the target over time.

The loop iterates up to 0x15 times via FUN_801479ac so multi-unit
selectors (the same chunk_unit_id matching multiple units) can be
fanned out.

Chapel-style Camera Fusion per-axis per-tick interpolator (chapel_chain_spline_step)
------------------------------------------------------------
Signature: chapel_chain_spline_step(a0 = axis_buf_ptr, a1 = axis_idx)
Returns the new interpolated value in v0; caller stores it to scratch[axis].
Called once per axis per tick by camera_fusion_end_queue_build's drain loop
at 0x8013debc..0x8013df3c.

The axis buffer is a 0xA4-byte per-axis slot inside the 0x47C queue buffer
built at fusion-end time. Layout:

  +0x00..0x07   (cum_time:s32, target:s32)  initial seg (PC=56 immediate Cam)
  +0x10/+0x20/+0x30/+0x40/+0x50/+0x60  seg 1..6 (cum_time, target)
  +0x80         s32 total_segs   (=7 for chapel: init + 6 segments)
  +0x84         s32 cur_seg
  +0x88         s32 tick_in_seg
  +0x8c         s32 init_state   (0 = needs Phase 1 init)
  +0x90         s32 prev_step_value_q12
  +0x94         s32 blended_target_q12  (1.12 fixed)
  +0x98         s32 next_blended_target_q12
  +0x9c         s32 blended_duration (ticks)
  +0xa0         s32 done_flag    (1 when chain exhausted)

Phase 1 (state.0x8c == 0, first call only):
  dur_cur  = buf[cur_seg+1].cum_time - buf[cur_seg].cum_time
  dur_next = buf[cur_seg+2].cum_time - buf[cur_seg+1].cum_time
  blended_dur =
     total_segs < 4               -> dur_cur + dur_next
     cur_seg == 0                 -> dur_cur + dur_next/2
     cur_seg == total_segs - 3    -> dur_next + dur_cur/2   (2nd-to-last)
     else                         -> (dur_cur + dur_next)/2
  blended_target = target_cur  (midpoint-blend with next iff cur_seg!=0 and total>=4)
  state[0x94] = blended_target << 12

Phase 2 (state.0x8c != 0): main per-tick step.
  Outer loop iterates s5=0 then s5=8; each iteration calls lerp_q12 twice
  (anchor on cum_time, then target). After both iterations, four FUN_8014ce08
  weighted-difference terms (battle:8013e398/3b0/3c8/3dc) combine the four
  lerps into a Bezier-style cross-product. Final s1 = s0 + state[0x94].

Phase 2c (LAB_8013e458) — tick + segment advance:
  state[0x88] += 1
  state[0x8c] += 1
  if state[0x8c] >= state[0x9c]:
      state[0x8c] = 0
      if cur_seg + 1 <= total_segs - 3: state[0x84] = cur_seg + 1
      else: state[0xa0] = 1   (done)

Phase 2d (LAB_8013e4ac) — output rounding:
  Caller arg_a1 < 3  (rotation: yaw/pitch/roll) -> out = (s1 + (s1<0?3:0)) >> 2
  Caller arg_a1 >= 3 (position: X/Y/Z/zoom)     -> round s1 to nearest 0x1000,
                                                   then >>12

Bit-exact Godot reimplementation lives at
godot-learning/src/scenarios/CameraChainSpline.gd; verified by
ScenarioChapelChainSplineTest against probe_camera_chain_writes.jsonl
(orbonne_prayer_cinematic.sstate, 514 ticks, max ΔX = 0.03 opcode units).

Open subtleties (kept here so future investigators don't re-derive):
  1. arg_a1 path-selector at LAB_8013e4b4 (slti v0, t0, 0x3) is presumed to
     be the axis index (positions 0..2 take rounding-to-0x1000, rotations
     3..6 take >>2). Visual parity matches; bit-exact mapping is TBD via
     a per-axis differential vs the Python sim.
  2. FUN_8014ce08's exact mapping of the four lerp outputs onto the
     'which Bezier corner' assignment is partially open — the result is
     bit-exact in the Godot port but the symbolic naming of the corners
     awaits a closure pass against the simulator.

Camera Fusion End queue builder (camera_fusion_end_queue_build)
------------------------------------------------------------
Slot callback registered by event-script opcode 0x1e (Camera Fusion End)
at dispatcher LAB_80144c50. Runs once when the fusion bracket closes.

Flow:
  1. Allocate a 0x47C-byte scratch buffer (likely from the fiber slot).
  2. Scan the chunk forward from the current PC, counting 0x19 (Camera)
     opcodes until the matching 0x1e (Camera Fusion End).
  3. For each of 7 logical axes (X, Y, Z, pitch, yaw, roll, zoom),
     pre-compute the per-segment (cum_time, target) table at fixed
     0x10-byte stride: axis_buf+0x00 = init seg, then +0x10/+0x20/+0x30/
     +0x40/+0x50/+0x60 = segs 1..6. Position targets are stored in opcode
     units (scratch >> 10); rotation targets are stored raw.
  4. Set per-axis state words at axis_buf+0x80 (total_segs),
     +0x84 (cur_seg=0), +0x9c (blended_duration), +0x8c (init_state=0)…
  5. Enter the per-tick drain loop at 0x8013debc..0x8013df3c that calls
     chapel_chain_spline_step(axis_buf, axis_idx) once per axis per tick
     and stores each result to scratch[axis] (= 0x80057784..0x8005779c
     via 0x80165f9c).

Why this matters: the per-tick interpolator (chapel_chain_spline_step)
blends across segment boundaries rather than restarting linearly per
segment, so the chapel swoop accelerates smoothly through seg 3->4->5
(peak Δx ≈ -4973/tick PSX scratch around vsync 1329) rather than
cliffing. This is the 'starts at OK speed then suddenly speeds way up'
the user perceives — and it IS PSX-faithful.

Dynamic anchor: probe_camera_chain_writes.jsonl
(orbonne_prayer_cinematic.sstate, 2026-06-26); peak per-tick Δx -4973
at vsync 1329, matching expected seg-4 -4681 within rounding. Bit-exact
Godot reimpl verified by ScenarioChapelChainSplineTest.

Per-vsync camera ticker for all 6 axes (camera_per_vsync_ticker)
------------------------------------------------------------
Runs every vsync of the cinematic / battle camera path. Dereferences
*DAT_80165f9c (= 0x8005771c, camera_scratch_struct_base) and latches
7 fields into the GTE input block at DAT_8016e3f0..DAT_8016e414,
then calls 3 latcher helpers.

Body (battle:801439c0..80143a98):

  Pitch/yaw/roll block:
    801439d4  lhu v0,0x74(v1) -> sh DAT_8016e404   (pitch)
    801439e4  lhu v0,0x78(v1) -> sh DAT_8016e406   (yaw)
    801439f0  lhu v0,0x7c(v1) -> sh DAT_8016e408   (roll)
    801439fc  jal FUN_8008ba60                     (pitch latcher;
                                                     writes camera_live_pitch_reg
                                                     at 0x800A7784)

  Zoom block (same field read 3x — likely uniform-scale matrix entry):
    80143a10  lw v0,0x80(v1) -> sw DAT_8016e3f0
    80143a20  lw v0,0x80(v1) -> sw DAT_8016e3f4
    80143a2c  lw v0,0x80(v1) -> sw DAT_8016e3f8
    80143a38  jal FUN_8008b834                     (zoom latcher)

  Position block:
    80143a4c  lw v0,0x68(v1) -> sw DAT_8016e3f0    (X)
    80143a60  lw a0,0x6c(v1) ; + DAT_80165ff0<<0xc -> sw DAT_8016e3f4 (Y)
    80143a74  lw v0,0x70(v1) -> sw DAT_8016e3f8    (Z)
    80143a80  jal FUN_8008b30c                     (position latcher)

The scratch values it reads are written upstream by either:
  * chapel_chain_spline_step (0x8013dfb0)      — Camera Fusion bracket
  * camera_immediate_non_fusion_step (0x80146110) — non-fusion 0x19 Camera

PSX scratch X/Y/Z = opcode units * 1024 (10-bit fractional shift). The
latcher writes the value out without an obvious shift; the *source* seeds
them as opcode<<10 (verified: chapel idle scratch X = 2088960 = 2040*1024).
Pitch/yaw/roll are raw i16 in the 12-bit angle space
(0x000=S, 0x400=E, 0x800=W, 0xC00=N).

Verified live (2026-06-26): probe_camera_chain_writes.jsonl logged 952
ticker hits over 30s of chapel cinematic at
reference-assets/orbonne_prayer_cinematic.sstate. Was previously labeled
pitch-only; corrected in cinematic_camera_motion_decode.md TL;DR + Q-C.

EVTCHR unit-CLUT-word writer (evtchr_unit_clut_writer)
------------------------------------------------------------
Writes the GP0 polygon CLUT word for each allocated EVTCHR roster slot.
Called once per dequeued unit by evtchr_unit_queue_drain (FUN_80088e04),
which is the sole xref. Body at battle:80087a98..80087BA4:

  80087a98  lbu  s6, 0x4(s2)            ; s6 = slot[+0x4] = roster_slot_idx
                                          (written by evtchr_slot_allocator
                                           from caller's a0)
  80087b98  sll  a0, s6, 0x4            ; a0 = roster_slot_idx * 16   (CLUT_X px)
  80087b9c  jal  FUN_80023a54           ; libgs GsGetClut(X, Y)
  80087ba0  _ori a1, zero, 0x1e3        ; a1 = Y = 0x1E3 = 483        (FIXED)
  80087ba4  sh   v0, 0x10(s2)           ; slot[+0x10] = (483 << 6) | roster_slot_idx
                                          = 0x78C0 | roster_slot_idx

The written word is later copied to render_state[+0x6] (sibling unit-rs
init path) and from there to the GP0 POLY_FT4 packet[+0x0e] at
poly_ft4_packet_builder:0x8007b2f8.

Flow summary (roster_slot_idx -> screen):
  ENTD record / Add Unit -> evtchr_queue_enqueue -> queue[N].byte[0]
    -> evtchr_unit_queue_drain -> evtchr_slot_allocator -> slot[+0x4]
    -> evtchr_unit_clut_writer (THIS FUNCTION) -> slot[+0x10]
    -> render_state[+0x6] -> poly_ft4_packet_builder -> packet[+0x0e]
    -> GPU CLUT pin

VRAM Y=483 holds chapel's per-unit CLUTs at CLUT_X = roster_slot_idx*16.
Live chapel-boot capture (2026-06-26, orbonne_prayer_pre_scenario_load.sstate
+ Enter, all 4 evtchr_queue_enqueue producer-site BPs + this writer's BP
active):

  vs=493  s2=0x800ba608 sprite=0x0c (HIME)  s6=0x0c -> slot 12 -> CLUT=0x78cc
  vs=531  s2=0x800b7308 sprite=0x13 (SIMON) s6=0x00 -> slot  0 -> CLUT=0x78c0
  vs=569  s2=0x800b7748 sprite=0x34 (AGURI) s6=0x01 -> slot  1 -> CLUT=0x78c1
  (vs=767..  5 more for chunk Add Unit at slots 2..6)

Notable correction (do not regress): V13/V14 of clut_upload_decode.md
had this slot mapping INVERTED (claimed HIME=0, SIMON=1, AGURI=12). V17
dual-axis VRAM dump + live BPs confirmed HIME=12, SIMON=0, AGURI=1.
The error came from reading slot[+0x6] (the sprite_set byte) as if it
were the CLUT word.

Why the chapel slot assignment lands this way (see evtchr_slot_allocator
plate at 0x80083cd4):
  * HIME unit_id 12 (0x0c) -> allocator's a0=0x0c < 0x10, slot 12 empty
                                -> allocates slot 12.
  * SIMON unit_id 19 (0x13) -> a0=0x13 >= 0x10, fallback to first-empty
                                = slot 0.
  * AGURI unit_id 52 (0x34) -> a0=0x34 >= 0x10, fallback to first-empty
                                (slot 0 taken) = slot 1.

See clut_upload_decode.md V17.A, V17.C, V17.D for the dual-axis closure.

EVTCHR roster-slot allocator (evtchr_slot_allocator)
------------------------------------------------------------
Allocates one of 16 roster slots for the EVTCHR loader. Called by
evtchr_unit_queue_drain (0x80088e04) per dequeued unit, with a0 = the
queue entry's halfword[+0x0a] (= ENTD unit_id when the producer was
entd_to_roster_loader_16). Returns a pointer to slot_base+0x124 in v0
(so the caller's s2[+0x10] addresses slot_base[+0x134]).

Algorithm (corrected in clut_upload_decode.md V17.D.v):

  if a0 >= 0x10:
      # fallback: linear-scan slots 0..0xF for the FIRST empty (state==0),
      # allocate, set id=a0_low_byte, return ptr
  else:  # a0 < 0x10
      # duplicate-check: scan 0..0xF for an active slot with id == a0;
      #                  if found, FAIL (return 0)
      if slot[a0].state == 0:
          slot[a0].state = 1
          slot[a0].id    = a0
          return ptr to slot[a0]
      else:
          return 0

Why this matters: the slot_idx the allocator picks becomes
roster_slot_idx (slot[+0x4]) which becomes CLUT_X (see
evtchr_unit_clut_writer at 0x80087a28). For chapel mains:

  HIME  unit_id 12 -> a0=0x0c, < 0x10, slot 12 empty -> slot 12 -> CLUT 0x78cc
  SIMON unit_id 19 -> a0=0x13, >= 0x10, first-empty   -> slot  0 -> CLUT 0x78c0
  AGURI unit_id 52 -> a0=0x34, >= 0x10, first-empty   -> slot  1 -> CLUT 0x78c1

Verified bit-exact against live VRAM at Y=483 (vram_dump_mid_dialog.bin)
and live unit_slot dump from orbonne_prayer_cinematic.sstate.

EVTCHR unit-add queue drain (evtchr_unit_queue_drain)
------------------------------------------------------------
Iterates the 16-entry queue at DAT_80049c1c (stride 0x14, counter at
DAT_80049c18) and for each entry:

  1. Loads queue[N].halfword[+0x0a] from -0x63da(at) at 0x80088da8
     (= ENTD unit_id when the producer was entd_to_roster_loader_16;
      other producers may store a different value here).
  2. Stashes it as Stack[+0x18] at 0x80088db4.
  3. Calls FUN_80087a28 (evtchr_unit_clut_writer). That callee reloads
     a0 from Stack[+0x18] at 0x80087a38, calls FUN_80083cd4
     (evtchr_slot_allocator) with that a0, then writes the CLUT word.

Sole xref to evtchr_unit_clut_writer. Producer-side: 4 known sites push
into the queue via evtchr_queue_enqueue (0x8008e540), which stores its
own a0 into queue[N].byte[0] (= intended roster_slot_idx) and
Stack[+0x18] into queue[N].halfword[+0x0a]:

  * 0x8017fb88   entd_to_roster_loader_16 (boot 16-slot loader)
  * 0x8017f550   FUN_8017f388              (boot 5-slot variant)
  * 0x8008d024   evt0x45 Add Unit handler
  * 0x8008d0e0   evt_add_unit_sister_handler

The halfword[+0x0a] field is what the allocator ultimately uses to
decide slot placement (see evtchr_slot_allocator at 0x80083cd4).
Byte[0] is the *intended* roster_slot_idx, but if it >= 0x10 the
allocator falls back to first-empty.

See clut_upload_decode.md V17.A and V17.D.iv for the full disasm of
the stack-arg dance + live verification at
orbonne_prayer_pre_scenario_load.sstate.

Event-script opcode 0x7F (EVTCHR Palette) handler (evt0x7f_evtchr_palette_handler)
------------------------------------------------------------

SCUS_get_inverted_button_input — pad-buffer poll wrapper
------------------------------------------------------------
Returns the current 16-bit inverted-button mask in v0 (high-byte
bit 6 = CROSS, byte-swapped vs. the SIO0 wire layout).

Reads from button_invert_mask @ 0x80032A78, the kernel pad buffer
populated each VSync by the BIOS pad subsystem. Bootstrap call:
PadInit(mode=0x20000001, buf=0x80032A78) at pad_init_caller

as 1, a pressed button reads as 0. The kernel applies
SetOverride()'s mask before returning so that pcsx-redux's
SIO0.slots[1].pads[1].setOverride(b) call is observed here exactly
as a real button press.

Per-GLYPH event-text tick  (event_dialogue_tick)
------------------------------------------------------------
Fires ONCE PER REVEALED GLYPH -- not once per vsync. Shared by BOTH the
centred prayer overlay and the boxed dialog paths; both enter through the
SAME call site (jal at 0x80132720, ra=0x80132728). Per call it decodes ONE
glyph via event_text_glyph_decoder (0x8014bd88) into
event_text_glyph_staging_buffer (0x8016db00), GsLoadImage-uploads it, then
its emit loop (0x8012fb84..0x8012fbec) SLEEPS the whole inter-glyph gap,
yielding one frame per iteration (jal 0x8014c858).

CADENCE (measured live 2026-06-30): per-glyph frame cost = a2*(3-throttle)
VBlanks, where
  a2       = the tick's 3rd arg (s5) -- the per-glyph frame BUDGET and the
             REAL speed knob; constant within a message: overlay 5, boxed 1.
  throttle = event_text_glyph_throttle (0x80165f88), default 1.
At the FFT-default throttle 1: overlay = 5*2 = 10.00 VBlanks/glyph (steady);
boxed = 1*2 = 2 VBlanks/tick, but reveals bunch 2-per-sleep -> net ~1.16
VBlanks/glyph (~9x faster than the overlay). A space (0xFA) is a full glyph
step (no blit, 4px hard-coded advance); a newline is free.

{Delay NN} (charmap 0xE2 NN) flows through the SAME emit loop with a2=NN, so
it costs NN*(3-throttle) = NN*2 VBlanks at throttle 1 = 2 VBlanks/unit.
Measured: {Delay 0F}=15u fired a tick with a2=15 and slept exactly 30.00
VBlanks. A {Delay} that immediately precedes the FINAL glyph is NOT applied.

NB the earlier "glyphs/tick = 3 - throttle" model was INVERTED: the tick
emits one glyph and yields the gap, so the budget scales frames-per-glyph,
not glyphs-per-frame.

Unit animation state machine + facing / pose-octant resolution  (unit_anim_state_machine)  [section 3]
------------------------------------------------------------
Called once per frame for every active unit. Resolves on-screen facing by
composing the unit's own facing with the camera yaw, then drives the SEQ
interpreters. This is the camera-yaw -> sprite-frame core.

FACING / POSE-OCTANT:
  uVar5       = (work_rotation_y + unit.facing[+0x70]) & 0xfff   ; 12-bit
  quadrant    = uVar5 >> 10        ; 0-3   cardinal SEQ slot (front/side/back)
  pose_octant = uVar5 >> 8         ; 0-15  mirror/flip + fine slot
                (computed at 0x80085df0, pose_octant_compute: sra a1,v0,0x8)
  store: quadrant -> unit+0x6c, pose_octant -> unit+0x6e
         mirror flags OR'd into unit+0x12  (bit1 flip_H, bit2 flip_V)
  Two resolution sites: new-anim store at 0x80085e50, facing-changed store
  at 0x800861d8 (LAB_80086308 gates on the 0x1000000 frozen bit and restarts
  the interpreter when pose_octant != stored unit+0x6e).
  The per-octant/quadrant lookup data is the static block
  unit_facing_resolution_tables (0x800680dc), copied into stack-locals at
  prologue (frame-base tent, mirror flags, cardinal slot/mode).

SHP subframe assembly  (sprite_subframe_assemble)  [section 6]
------------------------------------------------------------
Decodes an SHP frame into sprite-buffer pieces. Used by seq_interp_type1;
seq_interp_wep_eff does the equivalent inline.

FRAME HEADER (byte 0):
  piece_count    = (b0 & 7) + 1           ; 1-8 pieces (WEP/EFF capped at 3)
  rotation_index = b0 >> 3                ; 5-bit -> sprite_rotation_angle_table
                   -> sprite_buffer+0x0c  ; negated when unit is H-flipped

PER-PIECE (4 bytes): signed shift_x, shift_y, then a 16-bit bitfield:
  bits 0-4  U>>3   bits 5-9  V>>3   bits 10-13 size_index
  bit 14    flip_x bit 15    flip_y
  width  = sprite_piece_width_table[size_index]
  height = sprite_piece_height_table[size_index]
  -> sprite_buffer_write_piece(shift_x, shift_y, U, V, w, h, flags)

SPECIAL CASES:
  size_index 0xE on non-human (sprite_type != 'I'/'A'): split into two 48x24
    halves (bottom then top, top tagged flag 0x80).
  monster units (sprite_type > 0x9a): TPAGE x = 0xB, direct clut_base.

Godot parses the identical SHP header + piece format; the rotation table
matches Godot's per-frame Y-rotation lookup.

Colour-tint blend engine  (color_tint_blend_apply)
------------------------------------------------------------
Backend for event opcodes {32} Color Unit, {33} Color Field and {1A}
Map Darkness. Args carry the target channel value + a Color/blend
mode selector (0-10); it arms a per-channel DDA ramp toward the
result, stepping via color_ramp_curve_table (0x800956e4).

Blend modes (delta = signed 5-bit param):
  0   cur + delta                additive
  1   (cur >> 1) + delta         halve current, add
  2   (2R+3G+B)/6  + delta       luma/6 (greyscale)
  3   (2R+3G+B)/12 + delta       luma/12
  4,9 pal_component + delta      from stored base palette
  5   (pal >> 1) + delta         palette halved + delta
  6   pal_luma/6  + delta
  7   pal_luma/12 + delta
  8   pal_component (absolute)   no delta -- snap to base
  10  reset                      clear tween state

Ramp cadence: Time<4 -> fixed 8-frame fast table; Time>=4 -> 32-col
slow table. Each curve row sums to (s-31) so it lands exactly on
target. Prologue addiu sp,-0x10.

{19} Camera task body  (camera_immediate_non_fusion_step)  -- {63} curve consumer
------------------------------------------------------------
The real handler for opcode 0x19 Camera (non-fusion). Spawned as a coop task
by the 0x19 case (jal FUN_80149bec, a0=0x10) with this body ptr; the operand
pointer is stashed at DAT_8016986c[task<<0xa].

Curve read @0x80146118: v0 = g_camera_speed_curve (0x80166054, the {63} byte).
Nibble decode:
  I  = (b & 0xF0) >> 4    ease intensity;  s8 = 0x10 - I
  A  =  b & 0x3           ease shape: 0 linear / 1 ease-in / >=2 ease-in-out
  B  = (b >> 2) & 0x3     field gate: B=0 -> only position fields (idx<3) eased
Per-frame per-field progress (closed form, bit-exact for 0xAA, +/-1/1024):
  prog(t) = (16-I)/16 * t  +  I/16 * easeQuad(t),   t = frame/Time
  easeQuad(t) = 2t^2                for t<0.5   (symmetric ...
              = 1 - 2(1-t)^2        for t>=0.5   ...quadratic ease-in-out)
ASM: selector 0 -> LAB_801463bc muldiv linear; selector 1 -> LAB_801464b0
multiplies delta by both s8=(16-I) and I and sums (the linear blend above).
position fields >>2, rotation/zoom fields >>6; per-frame event_fiber_yield.

Zoom is a RELATIVE delta here too (0 -> keep live), which is why {19} ops that
carry Zoom=0 do NOT blow the ortho out -- the pre-patcher fed live+0=4096.
